classification: derived conditional dependency, not a numbered source theorem restatement
exact_header:
theorem stronglyConvex_minimum_growth {E : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    (f : E → EReal) (V : Set E) (lam : ℝ)
    (hf : SourceProper f) (hV : Convex ℝ V)
    (hdom : V ⊆ effectiveDomain f) (hlam : 0 ≤ lam)
    (hstrong : ∀ x ∈ V, ∀ y ∈ V, ∀ a : ℝ, 0 < a → a < 1 →
      f (a • x + (1 - a) • y) ≤
        (a : EReal) * f x + ((1 - a : ℝ) : EReal) * f y -
          (((lam / 2) * a * (1 - a) * ‖x - y‖ ^ 2 : ℝ) : EReal))
    (p : E) (hp : p ∈ V) (hmin : IsMinOn f V p)
    (q : E) (hq : q ∈ V) :
    (f p).toReal + (lam / 2) * ‖q - p‖ ^ 2 ≤ (f q).toReal
source_and_Lean_delta: Orabona, Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization, arXiv:1912.13213v10. This is a derived conditional consequence of Definition4.1 (printed34/PDF46), with properness from Definition2.18 (printed16/PDF28), generalized from the source finite-dimensional setting to an arbitrary real normed space. It is not a direct restatement of Lemma7.1.
boundary: This inequality assumes a supplied feasible minimizer. It does not prove existence or uniqueness of a minimum, construct a cumulative FTRL or BTRL trajectory, or establish a regret bound. The FTRL telescoping identity in Lemma 7.1, the source-support obligation for Theorem 6.9, and the corrected terminal terms in Theorems 7.47 and 15.31 remain separate. Chapter 2 and the book remain incomplete.
native_proof: SourceProper excludes negative infinity, while V is contained in effectiveDomain f, excluding positive infinity on V. Thus f(p) and f(q) are finite, and their real values preserve order. Set c = (λ/2)‖q − p‖² and g = f(q) − f(p) ≥ 0. Suppose g < c. Then c > 0 and a = (g + c)/(2c) lies strictly between 0 and 1. Convexity places a p + (1 − a)q in V. Minimality and strong convexity give f(p) ≤ a f(p) + (1 − a)f(q) − c a(1 − a). Composing these extended-real inequalities and converting their finite endpoints yields 0 ≤ (1 − a)(g − ca). But ca = (g + c)/2 > g and 1 − a > 0, a contradiction. If λ = 0 or p = q, the nonnegative gap cannot be smaller than c = 0.
